 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 13/10/2017,
PASSED IN MVC NO.235/2017, ON THE FILE OF THE V ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MACT, SHIVAMOGGA, SITTING AT SAGAR,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant, being dis-satisfied with the compensation of Rs.10,41,550/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries :
a) Left lower leg crush injury;
b) Cut lacerated wound on scalp with skin plap;
c) Fracture of frontal bone d) Head injury.
4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation :
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (Rs.)
 1. Pain and suffering 80,000/-
 2. Loss of income during treatment 24,000/-
 period

Sundar Devadiga vs Ganapati on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125158213/
2  3.

Medical expenses 5,71,000/-
 4. Loss of future earning 2,80,800/-
 5. Loss of future amenities 25,000/-
 6. Attendant charges 10,000/-
 7. Nourishment, diet and 20,750/-
 conveyance  8.

For removal of implant 30,000/-
 Total 10,41,550/-
5.
The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 30% to the whole body.
Three Doctors were examined on behalf of the claimant.

6. The Disability Certificate produced indicated that the claimant had difficulty in speech, decreased active range of movement of left ankle; difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, walking slope, standing on both lower limbs, standing on the left lower limb and squatting.
It was also noticed that swelling and scarring of left leg.
The Doctors, therefore, assessed the disability at 25% with respect to speech and 61% with respect to his left lower limb.
7. The claimant was directed to be present before this Court and accordingly he is present today.
It is noticed that the claimant is bound to a wheel chair and his left leg is deformed completely.
It is also noticed that he indeed has difficulty in talking.
Having regard to these facts and also the medical evidence adduced, it would be appropriate to determine the functional disability of the claimant at 60%.
8. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
9. Since the claimant has suffered disability at 60% to the whole body, 25% is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects.

Hence, the monthly income of the deceased for the purpose of determining towards 'loss of future income' would thus be Rs.11,250/- [Rs.9,000/- +
(Rs.9,000/- x 25%)].
10.
As the claimant was aged 46 years, a multiplier of '13' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.10,53,000/-* (Rs.11,250/- x 12 x '13' X 60%*) towards 'loss of future income'.
11.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,71,000/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.30,000/-
towards 'removal of plants', which is just and proper and is affirmed.
*Corrected/Inserted vide chamber order dated 02/06/2023.

Sundar Devadiga vs Ganapati on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125158213/
3
12. The evidence on record indicates that claimant was hospitalised for 90 days.
Having regard to the fact that he was hospitalised for 96 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards conveyance, nutrition and attendant charges.
13. The claimant has been awarded a sum of Rs.24,000/- as 'loss of income during treatment period'.

Since the claimant was hospitalised for 96 days, it would be appropriate to determine the laid-up period as 7 months and accordingly a sum of Rs.63,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 7 months) would be awarded towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
14. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant has suffered a severe deformity to his leg and is bound to a wheel chair, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities.

15. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings', having regard to the fact that the claimant was hospitalised for 96 days and has suffered a severe deformity, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings.
16. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 1,50,000/-
 2. Loss of income during 63,000/-
 treatment period  3. Medical expenses 5,71,000/-
 4. Loss of future earning 10,53,000/-*
 5. Loss of future amenities 1,50,000/-
 6. Conveyance, Nutrition and 1,00,000/-
Attendant charges
8. For removal of implant 30,000/-

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.21,17,000/-* as against Rs.10,41,550/-
*Corrected vide chamber order dated 02/06/2023. along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
18. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

19. Out of the compensation amount, 60% of the amount shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalised Bank in the name of claimant, as per his choice, for a period of five years with a liberty Sundar Devadiga vs Ganapati on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125158213/
4
to withdraw the interest accrued periodically.
After maturity, the amount shall be directly paid to the petitioner without any further proceedings; remaining 40% of the amount shall be released in favour of claimant.
20. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
